rationale: The Old English verb *aþrýtan* (cf. Latin *taedere* / *pertaesum esse*) typically denotes the sense of being wearied *of* something — becoming bored, disgusted, or fed up — rather than physical exhaustion, aligning with tire.v.01 ("lose interest or become bored"). The grammatical gloss context in Ælfric (Gr. 33) supports a mental/affective weariness rather than bodily fatigue.
